html:
A giant oil field under the shallow northern Caspian Sea, off the coast of Kazakhstan near Atyrau. It was found in 2000 and was then the largest oil discovery in decades. Recoverable reserves are put at about 13 billion barrels.

Getting the oil out proved very hard. The sea there freezes in winter, the oil sits deep under high pressure and the gas that comes with it is full of poisonous hydrogen sulphide. Workers built artificial islands to drill from. Output started in 2013, stopped within weeks when pipelines leaked, and only resumed in 2016. The cost ran far over plan, which makes it one of the most expensive oil projects ever.

Kashagan sits beside the older Tengiz field. Together they made oil the base of the economy of independent Kazakhstan, with much of it shipped west through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium to the Black Sea.
